column1: # TWO-ASPECT tier-1 demo board -- 2026-08-28 hq_P -- row bench-rep-loop-demo-harness
# Produced by SCRIP/scripts/bench_rep_loop_demos_snobol4.sh (SCRIP f93ba644). Re-run it; never hand-edit.
# ⛔ ASPECT 1 is a TOTAL (carries startup+compile); ASPECT 2 is a SLOPE (match only). Per the FACT RULE
# they may NEVER share a column, and they DISAGREE IN DIRECTION here -- that disagreement is the result.
# ⭐ WHAT THE TWO ASPECTS SAY, AND THEY SAY OPPOSITE THINGS -- m4 vs the clean oracle:
#   ASPECT 1 (whole process): we lose EVERY row. 3-6x behind on the small demos.
#   ASPECT 2 (match only):    claws5-match 1.686x AHEAD, treebank-match-fence 1.194x AHEAD,
# ⛔ THE READING: on the small demos our loss is dominated by STARTUP+COMPILE, not by matching -- and our
# match engine is already AHEAD on claws5 and treebank-fence. json is the outlier and it is not close:
# its MATCH phase alone is 11.6x behind, which no whole-process number could have told us (aspect 1 has
# json-match at 9.08 vs 1.94 ms = 0.21x, a fifth of the real match-phase gap).
# ⭐ json-match's match phase is the single worst number in the tier-1 set and was INVISIBLE before tonight.
# ⚠️ TWO ROWS REFUSED AND ARE PRINTED AS REFUSALS, NOT DROPPED: treebank-match/sbl and
# claws5-match-fence/m4 did not converge by reps=4,000,000. Their neighbours converged, so this is a
# per-arm instability to chase, not a harness-wide fault. A refusal is the honest output; a number taken
# from an unconverged ramp would have been wrong by up to 13x (see the harness header's own measurement).
